sections.h2: Where is the Cumberland County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The office sits in Room 114 of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse, 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville, and the land records line is 910-678-7775. The office keeps its own website at ccrod.org, where the posted office hours and the yearly holiday schedule live.

Cumberland County's land records reach back to 1754, which the office describes as the official start of the county. The same counter also handles notary oaths, birth, death and marriage records, and it records military discharge papers (DD-214) for retired service members at no charge.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed do when you sell a house in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
Recording puts your sale on the public record, and under North Carolina law a conveyance does not protect the buyer against lien creditors or other purchasers until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order in which instruments are registered, so the time stamp on a Cumberland County deed matters.

For a seller the practical steps are short:

  • Sign the deed in front of a notary before it goes to the office.
  • Make sure the deed carries the excise tax and the filing fee.
  • Ask whoever handles your closing to confirm the date and time the deed was filed.
  • Keep the recorded copy with the book and page reference for your own files.

The office itself cannot give legal advice or draft deeds, so questions about wording go to an attorney.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $26.00 for up to fifteen pages, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for up to thirty-five pages. The county's fee schedule follows the uniform statewide fees and lists the items below.

Cumberland County Register of Deeds fee schedule, as printed on ccrod.org
ItemFee printed
Deeds and instruments in general$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, then $4.00 per added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, then $4.00 per added page
Extra instrument in the same document$10.00
Non-standard document$25.00 on top of the recording fee
SatisfactionsNo fee
Certified copies$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Plat or map recording$21.00 per page
DD-214 recordingNo fee

Checks and money orders are made out to the Cumberland County Register of Deeds. Re-recording is charged as if it were the original filing.

sections.h2: How is the deed excise tax figured in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
The county's recording page prints the excise tax on deeds as $2.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, counting any fractional part, and the state statute words the same rate as $1.00 for each $500. The tax must be paid with the filing fee, and the amount is written on the front of the deed.

The state statute says the transferor, meaning the seller, pays the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Half of the money stays with the county general fund and half goes to the Department of Revenue. If your contract price is not a round number, ask your closing attorney for the exact figure rather than estimating at the counter.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Cumberland County office will accept it?
sections.html:
A North Carolina deed has to name the person who prepared it on the first page, and the first page should also show a return-to name and address. The office lists these points on its recording requirements page:

  • The draftsman line, usually written "Prepared by" or "Drawn by."
  • A "Return to" name and address on page one.
  • The excise tax or revenue amount on the front of the deed.
  • Paper size, margins, font size and page limits that meet state recording standards.
  • Notarization of the signatures before filing.

Satisfactions and UCC filings are exempt from the formatting rules. A deed that misses the standards can still be recorded, but the $25.00 non-standard fee is added.

sections.h2: How does the Property Notification service protect a Cumberland County owner?
sections.html:
It is a free email alert that tells you when a document with your name is filed at the Register of Deeds. The office promotes it as an early warning against deed fraud, and it asks owners who spot an unauthorized filing to contact a real estate attorney.

To sign up, go to ccrod.org, choose Records Search, then New Property Notification, and follow the prompts. The email gives the name matched, the filing date, the book and page, and a link to view the document. The office is clear that the service is not a guarantee against fraud. Owners of a vacant or inherited Fayetteville property may find the alerts useful while the house is empty.

sections.h2: How do deed records connect to Cumberland County property taxes?
sections.html:
The tax listing owner is set by reading the instruments indexed with the Register of Deeds and the Clerk of Court's estates division as of January 1 each year. Cumberland County runs a permanent listing system, so owners only report changes such as a new deck, an in-ground pool or a remodel, with forms asked back by January 31.

Listing forms go to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or to Room 530 of the courthouse. State law makes taxes due September 1, and interest starts on January 6 at two percent, followed by three-fourths of one percent a month from February 1. Ask Tax Administration how the current-year bill is handled when the house sells mid-year.

Owners with a service-connected disability can ask for the state exclusion on the first $45,000 of appraised value, filed with the county assessor. Cumberland County has a large veteran population, so that program comes up more often here than in most counties.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Cumberland County homes?
sections.html:
Cumberland County had an estimated 338,473 residents on July 1, 2025, living in 146,623 housing units across 652.56 square miles of land. Only 55.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $199,200.
  • Median gross rent: $1,222.
  • Households: 129,758, with 2.48 people per household.
  • Veterans living in the county: 40,226.
  • Median household income: $61,291 in 2024 dollars.

Those figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table and describe the whole county, not one Fayetteville street or neighborhood.

sections.h2: What should a Cumberland County seller check before the deed is signed?
sections.html:
Start with the loan. A satisfaction of a deed of trust is recorded with no county fee, so a paid-off mortgage should show a recorded release before or soon after closing. If payments are behind, North Carolina uses a power-of-sale process heard by the clerk of superior court, and after a foreclosure sale there is a ten-day window for upset bids that must top the price by at least five percent, with a $750.00 minimum increase.

Then look at the title. Search the county's land records for the last recorded deed, any liens and any deed of trust still open. Inherited houses call for a check of the clerk of court's estates division records as well. Selling to a cash buyer who takes the house as it is can shorten the checklist, but the deed, the excise tax and the recording fee still apply.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax when selling a house in Cumberland County?
faqs.a: The seller, called the transferor in the statute, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Cumberland County's page prints the rate as $2.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, and the state statute words it as $1.00 per $500.

faqs.q: How much does the Cumberland County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A deed is $26.00 for up to fifteen pages, plus $4.00 for each page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for up to thirty-five pages. Satisfactions of a deed of trust carry no fee.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office states that North Carolina law bars it from giving legal advice or preparing deeds. A deed must be drafted, signed and notarized before it is brought in, and an attorney can answer wording questions.

faqs.q: What is the Property Notification service in Cumberland County?
faqs.a: It is a free service that emails you when a document with your name is filed at the Register of Deeds. You sign up through ccrod.org under Records Search, and the office says it is an early warning and no guarantee against fraud.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Cumberland County real property listing form?
faqs.a: Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or bring it to Room 530 of the courthouse. The county asks for forms by January 31 so changes reach that year's assessment.
